Abstract.AbstractText: Metabolic dysfunction has reemerged as an essential hallmark of tumorigenesis, and metabolic phenotypes are increasingly being integrated into pre-clinical models of disease. The complexity of these metabolic networks requires systems-level interrogation, and metabolic flux analysis (MFA) with stable isotope tracing present a suitable conceptual framework for such systems. Here we review efforts to elucidate mechanisms through which metabolism influences tumor growth and survival, with an emphasis on applications using stable isotope tracing and MFA. Through these approaches researchers can now quantify pathway fluxes in various in vitro and in vivo contexts to provide mechanistic insights at molecular and physiological scales respectively. Knowledge and discoveries in cancer models are paving the way toward applications in other biological contexts and disease models. In turn, MFA approaches will increasingly help to uncover new therapeutic opportunities that enhance human health.
